label: input h late in the original phase, in sequences starting with t/s/x/3/d
explanation: Token-specific feature. It fires almost only when the input is the letter h during the original phase at positions 4-8, which are late steps close to <DEL> (to_go 0-3). 96% of activation mass is on in_tok == h and 99.5% is in the original phase. It never fires in the copy phase and only trivially at <DEL>. Most h inputs do not trigger it, though: only about 3.5% of h at t >= 4 fire, and none at t <= 3. Whether it fires depends on earlier context. It is strongly enriched when the first original token is t (10.7x lift, 42% of mass), and also when it is s, x, 3 or d. A preceding k is also enriched (6.6x), and so are k, 0, j or h two steps back. The largest activations come from sequences that start with t and have d/k earlier, e.g. t c a d k k [h]. The predicate h, t>=4, first_tok in {t,s,x,3,d} recovers about 79% of mass at 16% precision. Plain h at t>=4 recovers 96% of mass at 3.5% precision. The contextual gating is fuzzy and I could not capture it with a simple predicate.

scorecard.summary: Weighted combination of 40 cues. Raise it: orig0=t (+5.49), orig0=s (+3.55), orig0=3 (+3.39), orig0=x (+3.19), prev_tok=k (+3.09), orig0=d (+2.91). Lower it: prev3_tok=- (-3.52), orig2=l (-2.55), t=3 (-2.50), prev_tok=x (-2.11).
